data/data-grid.notes:
```tsx
<DataGrid rows={rows} columns={columns} toolbar={{ csv: false, groups: false }} columnMenu={false} animate={false}
  empty={<EmptyState title="No orders yet" />}
  labels={{ search: "Find an order", rows: (n) => `${n} orders`, total: "Sum", filtersActive: (n) => `${n} filters on` }} />
```

`labels` keys: `search`, `tools`, `grouping`, `groupHint`, `showAll`, `filters`, `csv`, `noRows`, `noMatch`, `total`,
`emptyGroup`, `selectAll`, `selectRow`, `sortAsc`, `sortDesc`, `clearSort`, `group`, `ungroup`, `pinStart`, `pinEnd`,
`unpin`, `hide`, `sum`, `average`, `minimum`, `maximum`, `count`, `distinct`, and the functions `filtersActive(n)`,
`rows(n)`, `selected(n)`, `columnMenu(column)`, `resize(column)`. The texts inside filter controls and cell editors
belong to the table engine (`march/table`).

Column extras: `aggregate` is `"sum" | "avg" | "min" | "max" | "count" | "distinct"` or `(values, rows) => result`;
`groupable: false` hides "Group by this column". Every `createTable` column option works (`pin`, `width`, `format`,
`filter`, `editable`, `validate`, `render` …).

Shared engines it uses, each importable on its own: `createAxis` / `createViewport` (core/virtual), `createSelection` /
`moveCursor` (core/selection), `groupRows` / `aggregate` / `aggregates` (march/data), `pointerDrag`
(march/motion), `CellEditor` / `FilterControl` (march/table).
data/data-grid.a11y:
`role="grid"` with `aria-rowcount` / `aria-colcount` (the full size, not the rendered window), `aria-rowindex` /
`aria-colindex` on each row and cell, `aria-sort` on headers, `aria-selected` on rows, `aria-expanded` /
`aria-level` on group rows. The grid is one tab stop; the cursor cell is announced through `aria-activedescendant`.
Resize handles are separators with their current width. Motion (row entrance, column slide, save flash) runs on the
motion engine, so reduced motion and the global pause apply.

data/gantt.notes:
```tsx
<Gantt tasks={$tasks} names={false} help={false} todayLine={false} animate={false}
  barLabel={(task) => <>{task.name} · {Math.round((task.progress ?? 0) * 100)}%</>}
  labels={{ today: "Now", task: "Work item", days: (n) => `${n} days` }} />
```

Dates come from `core/date` (`diffDays`, `addDays`, `startOfWeek`, `dateFormat` …), drags from `pointerDrag`
(march/motion).
data/gantt.a11y:
Each bar is a button named with the task, its dates, progress and predecessors. One bar is in the tab order; ↑ ↓ move
between tasks, Enter selects, Alt+← → moves a task by a day and Alt+Shift+← → changes its end (mirrored in RTL); every
change is announced. Hovering or focusing a bar highlights its row and its arrows. The arrows draw themselves in, a
dropped bar settles with a spring and pushed tasks fade in at their new place — all on the motion engine, so reduced
motion and the global pause apply.

data/list-row.a11y:
The row is a real `<a>` or `<button>` when it navigates or acts; controls in `actions` are placed beside it, never
inside. A plain row takes the role its list needs (`option`, `menuitem`, `treeitem`, `radio` …) with `tabindex` and
`ref` for roving focus; keyboard handling belongs to the host list (Listbox, Menu, Tree). `selected` is announced by
the attribute that fits the role; `disabled` disables a button and sets `aria-disabled` elsewhere, and its click does
nothing. The focus ring is drawn inside the row. Scrolling text is read once and stops under reduced motion.

data/scheduler.a11y:
Month and time grids are `role="grid"` with column headers. Month days are one roving tab stop (arrows move, Enter
opens the day). Every event is a button whose name says title, day, time and place. Keyboard edits: Alt+arrows move
(↑ ↓ by `step` in the time grid, ← → by a day, mirrored in RTL), Alt+Shift+↑ ↓ resizes, PageUp / PageDown change the
period; each change is announced in a live region. Changing the period slides the grid in the direction of travel,
dropped events settle with a spring, all on the motion engine (reduced motion and global pause apply).

data/time-ruler.notes:
`timeTicks(duration, { step?, major?, minor? })` returns the computed ticks; `timePercent(ms, duration)` a CSS
percentage on the same scale. The CSS variable `--m-time-ruler-reach` makes the playhead line run below the ruler,
over the rows of a timeline.
data/time-ruler.a11y:
Read-only the ruler is decoration (`aria-hidden`): announce the time where it is written. Seekable: a `group` named
"Time ruler" whose playhead is a `slider` (value in ms, spoken through `valueText`); Left / Right move it by `keyStep`
(mirrored in right-to-left text, ten times with Shift), Home and End jump to the ends. The grip shows a focus ring;
reduced motion: no grip animation.

data/tree.a11y:
`role="tree"` with `treeitem`, `group`, `aria-level`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-selected`. Focus is on the
`treeitem` itself (its row shows the ring); one item is in the Tab order (roving focus, it returns to the last one): ↑ ↓ Home End move among visible rows, → opens (then goes to the first child), ← closes (then goes to the parent; the two swap in right-to-left), Enter or Space selects. The chevron turns
on the motion engine's duration tokens and the indent uses logical properties (RTL mirrors).

data/tree-view.a11y:
`role="tree"` with `aria-multiselectable`; rows are `treeitem`s with `aria-level`, `aria-setsize`, `aria-posinset`,
`aria-expanded`, `aria-selected` and `aria-busy` while loading. One tab stop; the cursor row is announced through
`aria-activedescendant`. Keys: ↑ ↓ Home End PageUp PageDown move, → opens / goes to the first child, ← closes / goes
to the parent (mirrored in RTL), Enter selects and opens or activates, Space selects (toggles in multiple mode),
Shift+arrows extend, Ctrl+A selects all, `*` opens the siblings, typing jumps to a matching label, Alt+↑ / Alt+↓
moves. Opening animates the new rows and a dropped node settles with a spring, on the motion engine (reduced motion and
global pause apply).

data/virtual-list.notes: Reads and writes are batched on the motion engine's frame (`measure`), never per scroll event.
data/virtual-list.a11y:
The rows are a `role="list"` of `listitem`s with `aria-posinset` / `aria-setsize`, so screen readers announce "row 41
of 10,000" even though only a window exists. Keep focusable content inside rows: Tab moves through the rendered rows
and the list scrolls to follow focus.
